title: Three 1 mm lumped ports at 10 GHz, 15 mm apart side by side and end to end: self resistance and mutual impedances
source: A gap carrying a uniform current is a Hertzian dipole: its radiation resistance is 80π²(l/λ)² and its field at the other gaps the exact field of the current elements (C. A. Balanis, Antenna Theory, 4th ed., Wiley 2016, eqs. 4-10, 4-19); the open-circuit voltage V₂ = −∫ E₁ · dl over the second gap, summed by 16 × 16 Gauss points in emcraft-theory (radiation::mutual_impedance_parallel)

quantities.quantity: Re Z11 of the driven gap (Ω; its current is 1 A, real, to 1e-8)
quantities.reason: the power the gap delivers, radiated through the layer: +0.2 % at six elements per wavelength (its reactance, the self-inductance of a filament, has no finite limit and is not compared)

quantities.quantity: Re Z21, side by side at 15 mm (Ω)
quantities.reason: second-order elements of λ/6, three between the gaps: −0.0045 Ω (complex error 2 % of |Z21|)
+0.0064 Ω; the near field's 1/r³ part is the hardest to resolve

quantities.quantity: Re Z31, end to end at 15 mm (Ω)
